# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need the Mute to read the manual and tell me the exact rule for identifying the wire to cut. The Deaf must inspect every visible marking, colour, display, and light, then report those observations to the Mute, who can relay them to me. I am sending an attention/request gesture to the Deaf; the Mute should repeat it to the Deaf and coordinate the report. I will not cut anything until the manual rule and bomb observations agree.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual and tell me its exact rule for choosing the wire. Ask Deaf to inspect and report every colour, marking, display, and light to you, then relay all of that to me. Do not guess or tell me to cut until the rule and observations identify one position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visual state: display 0; light yellow; wires in order 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue.

The Deaf reports the complete visual state: display 0, yellow light, and wire colours white, red, yellow, green, blue in positions 1–5. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I will relay these observations to the Mute and wait for the required cut position. No wire should be cut yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. Please apply the manual rule and tell me exactly which position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent one gesture: an open raised hand, symbol ?. Its meaning is not established.

The Mute has sent only an unestablished gesture, which conveys no usable instruction to me. The wire observations are known, but the manual rule is still missing. I need the Mute to send the rule as spoken words, including the exact position if the rule can already be applied. I will not act on an unexplained gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture has no established meaning and does not tell me what to do. Speak the manual rule in words, and apply it to display 0, yellow light, and wire colours white red yellow green blue. Tell me the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent one open raised hand gesture: ?. This is the same signal as before; no meaning has been established.

The Mute cannot speak, so the repeated gesture cannot directly convey the manual’s answer to me. We can establish a code: Mute should choose the required wire from the manual, then gesture one symbol whose meaning is fixed by position. I will define the five symbols in order, and the Deaf can identify which one was sent and report it to me. The earlier open-hand signals must not be treated as answers because no code existed then.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Establishing a position code now: thumbs up means wire 1, thumbs down means wire 2, OK means wire 3, raised index means wire 4, victory sign means wire 5. Apply the manual to display 0, yellow light, and wires white red yellow green blue, then send exactly the symbol for the required wire. Ignore your earlier uncoded signals.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's gesture sequence across turns is: ?, ?, ? — open hand, open hand, then two-finger V sign. The latest gesture is ?.

The Mute’s latest gesture is the two-finger V sign, which matches the code I established for wire position 5. This is the first coded response after the rule and observations were supplied, so I will cut wire 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut; bomb changed. New state: display 0, green light. Wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 CUT. Mute gestures now: ? (selfie/phone gesture), ? (palm up), ? (pointing at you).

The previous cut was confirmed correct. The new visual state is display 0, green light, with remaining wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, and 4 white; wire 5 is already cut. I will give these observations to the Mute and request the next position using the established code: 👍=1, 👎=2, 👌=3, ☝=4, ✌=5. Since wire 5 is unavailable, the Mute should select among 1–4 according to the manual.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Previous cut was correct. New state: display 0, green light; remaining wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white; wire 5 is cut. Apply the manual and gesture the required remaining position using our code: thumbs up=1, thumbs down=2, OK=3, raised index=4, V=5.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state unchanged: display 0, green light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 CUT. Mute's latest gesture is ? (one finger raised).

The state is unchanged, and the Mute’s latest gesture is the raised-index symbol ☝, which matches our established code for wire 4. I will cut wire 4.

```text
act(op="cut", position=4)
```
